 BASKETBALL Philadelphia 76ers A proud LeBron reacts to Bryce James' spectacular college play which went viral: “1% each day, young king”
 The 19-year-old delivered an impressive block during Arizona's victory over Northern Arizona

 A spectacular defensive play from Bryce James has given LeBron James another reason to celebrate his youngest son's basketball development, with the 19-year-old producing a viral moment during Arizona 's emphatic victory over Northern Arizona .
 Bryce delivered an impressive block at the rim as the Arizona Wildcats secured a 90-59 win on Tuesday, providing a glimpse of the athletic ability that has surrounded his basketball career with considerable attention.
 Bryce James opens Arizona exhibition with a first-possession 3-pointer The young guard finished with three points, two assists, two steals and a block in 13 minutes. Although his offensive contribution was modest, his defensive performance offered encouragement as he attempts to establish himself in coach Tommy Lloyd 's rotation.
 LeBron , who now plays for the Philadelphia 76ers , shared footage of the block on Instagram before posting additional highlights from his son's performance, accompanied by a message celebrating his progress.
 “Bryce James is starting to understand it now. 1% each day Young (king)!” LeBron wrote.
 The reaction highlighted the importance of gradual improvement for Bryce, whose college career has developed at a considerably different pace from that of his older brother, Bronny James .
 While Bronny entered the NBA after one season at USC, Bryce has taken a more measured approach, spending his first year with Arizona developing without appearing in regular-season games.
 During that campaign, the Wildcats won both the Big 12 regular-season and tournament championships before reaching the Final Four, giving Bryce an opportunity to experience a successful college program without immediately carrying significant playing responsibilities.
 Now a redshirt freshman, Bryce is beginning to receive opportunities under Lloyd , although his involvement remains limited. Through three appearances, he is averaging 2.7 points and 1.7 assists as he adjusts to competitive college basketball.
 His performance against Northern Arizona was particularly encouraging because of his defensive contributions, with the block and two steals demonstrating how he might earn additional minutes without becoming a major offensive option.
 The 6-foot-5 guard has shown flashes of similar ability before, including a memorable chase-down block during his time at Sierra Canyon that drew comparisons with his father's trademark defensive plays.
 Ver esta publicación en Instagram
 LeBron celebrates Bryce's progress
 Bryce 's breakthrough moment arrived on an otherwise disappointing evening for LeBron , whose Philadelphia team suffered a 123-101 defeat against the Boston Celtics .
 Despite the result, the four-time NBA champion made time to acknowledge his son's performance, continuing a pattern of publicly encouraging Bryce throughout his development.
 LeBron has repeatedly emphasized the importance of making small improvements, previously sharing similar messages when Bryce 's high school highlights attracted attention.
 That philosophy appears particularly relevant now that Bryce is competing for minutes within an established Arizona program rather than attempting to accelerate his journey towards the NBA.
 His immediate challenge is earning the trust of Lloyd and becoming a dependable contributor as the Wildcats progress through their schedule.
 The viral block may represent only one moment in a lengthy college season, but LeBron 's reaction suggests he values the progress behind it as much as the highlight itself.
